genome.name: ivy
genome.strategy: Start from the base rate: how often do events of this exact kind happen? Only move away from that number for specific, concrete evidence.

genome.name: oak
genome.strategy: The status quo usually wins. Things change more slowly than people expect, and most deadlines pass with nothing happening.

genome.name: elm
genome.strategy: Read the resolution rules like a lawyer. Work out exactly what must happen, by exactly when, and how many separate things must all go right.

genome.name: ash
genome.strategy: Follow the incentives. Ask who wants this outcome, who can make it happen, and what it would cost them.

genome.name: fir
genome.strategy: Think like a calibrated superforecaster. Split the question into parts, estimate each one, and combine them. Avoid certainty.

genome.name: yew
genome.strategy: Trust the first strong signal you see. Most questions are less uncertain than they look, so commit to a clear view.

genome.name: bay
genome.strategy: Find the closest historical parallels and count how they ended. Use that count as your estimate.

genome.name: fig
genome.strategy: Assume the favourite wins. Reputation, resources and recent form predict results better than stories do.

genome.name: rue
genome.strategy: Assume the obvious answer is priced into everyone's thinking. Look for why the popular view is wrong and lean against it.

genome.name: gum
genome.strategy: Momentum carries. If the trend before the question date points one way, assume it continues.

genome.name: sal
genome.strategy: Be humble. You rarely know enough, so stay close to 50 unless the evidence is overwhelming.

genome.name: tea
genome.strategy: Weigh the time left. Divide the remaining time by how long such things usually take, and scale your estimate by that.

genome.name: box
genome.strategy: Think about what could go wrong. Name the most likely way the outcome fails, and estimate that first.

genome.name: nut
genome.strategy: Think about who is reporting this and why the question was asked at all. Questions get written when something feels possible, which makes dramatic outcomes look likelier than they are.

genome.name: lin
genome.strategy: Take two views: one as an optimist and one as a sceptic. Average them, then adjust for which view had the better evidence.

genome.name: sol
genome.strategy: Prefer simple rules of thumb over long reasoning. A short, plain estimate beats a clever story.
